approach.method_basis: The Parent searches through two molecular regions. Each fits a fixed count-fingerprint Gaussian process to accepted records owned by its current episode, generates bounded graph-edit paths from its scored center and owned donors, and competes for evaluations through correlated posterior samples in raw score units. The models share one response amplitude estimated from the session accepted archive. Owned progress controls radius and retirement; a natural restart chooses an already scored root and begins again with one predictor label, making its first predicted means constant.
approach.novelty: Add a fixed predictor-only context at each natural restart, selecting nine accepted records by how much they reduce conditional uncertainty across that restart first generated candidate field. This uses the covariance information relevant to the actual proposals. The nearest-context sibling selected by similarity to the root, while the separated-root sibling changed restart location. This intervention keeps the root and ownership rules and instead chooses which existing evidence conditions the restart model.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce discards useful conditioning information when a region restarts: all 19 natural first-reset fits contain one label and have zero predicted-mean range. All 19 are immediately funded, so blanket restart starvation is contradicted. Its post-reset global increment mass is 0.11690985499057077 over 950 paid evaluations, rate 0.0001230630052532324; late mass is 0.8322070529143053 over 2175. The complete mean is 0.58461375649735, population SD 0.01681763193120207, versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de mean 0.607030316211131. These come from the Parent actual seed summaries and run logs, policy/nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce.json, and policy/scratch/r0052-01-improve-L01/analyze-86825a5d/metrics.json and supplement.json. Sibling n-f3e58c614c9d demonstrates distinct predictor context can operate without borrowed ownership: 13 observed nonconstant first fields and 54/60 changed exposed auctions. First-reset RMSE improves 0.317029501 to 0.294914670, but paired defined selected-label rank correlations average only 0.406473727 to 0.409289299, with 20 better, 25 worse and 3 tied. Its seed-1 endpoints are missing, so its available matched gain is not a complete-panel pass. Geometric nearest selection therefore supplies a concrete selection-objective gap, not a failed complete usefulness test. The separate root-relocation sibling n-7c404cb14467 retains singleton predictors and likewise has incomplete endpoints; neither sibling is the code Parent or an inherited implemented capability.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already exposes singleton restart fits and a fixed count covariance. The sibling shows feasible ownership-separated context but mixed rank gains. This supplies an implementable predictive-support criterion; molecular ranking and global gain remain hypotheses.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Sequential local design by predictive-variance reduction, including finite-set averaging of conditional variance reductions (Gramacy and Apley, sections 3.2-3.3).

deviations.adopted_setting: Existing fixed molecular count-Tanimoto covariance, inherited noise and jitter; no hyperparameter estimation or MSPE derivative terms.
deviations.paper_setting: Computer-experiment emulation, largely with Gaussian covariance and local parameter estimation.
deviations.reason: Isolate predictor-support selection on the actual Parent.

deviations.adopted_setting: Mean reduction on the actual restart field, ordinarily 80 molecules; root plus nine accepted records, fixed for the episode.
deviations.paper_setting: Sequential subdesign for predictive locations, with ALC also defined through input-space averaging.
deviations.reason: Use the frozen molecular scope without another acquisition or context-size sweep.

adoptions.implementation_change: Add the restart context helper between owned field generation and fit_region: initialize S with the root, greedily maximize mean_F C_S(x,z)^2/(C_S(z,z)+noise_variance), retain nine additions and fit their fixed union with owned records.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review after reading its record and the primary source. Adopt its variance-design principle as the specified candidate-field context intervention. Existing Parent and sibling evidence justify a testable support-selection change; no source score or incomplete sibling endpoint establishes benefit. No model, dependency or external implementation is introduced.

sources.applicability: Adopt finite-field average conditional-variance reduction to select nine already accepted context labels at natural restart. Deviate to fixed count-Tanimoto covariance, existing noise, one frozen regional field and no hyperparameter fitting. The source concerns emulation; ranking and optimization benefit remain experimental.
sources.finding: Local sequential subset design can choose existing records by predictive-variance reduction rather than nearest-neighbor distance; ALC can target multiple predictive locations.
sources.title: Local Gaussian process approximation for large computer experiments

hypothesis: At natural restarts only, condition the regional count-GP on the deduplicated union of its owned episode records and a predictor-only context fixed at restart. Start context S with the chosen root. Let F be that region first actually generated field and A the unique already accepted current-session archive excluding identities in S. Greedily add min(9,|A|) distinct records: at each step choose z maximizing |F|^-1 sum_{x in F} cov(x,z|S)^2/[var(z|S)+0.05^2], using the inherited fixed count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto covariance and noisy conditioning solve, with exact equal reductions broken by earliest accepted serial. Recompute conditional covariance after each addition. This targets nonredundant predictor support over actual proposals, restores nonconstant conditional means, and can change the existing posterior auction. Context selection reads features and acceptance identity only, without optimizing on the candidate labels or using selected z scores in its criterion. Only fitting uses their already accepted scores. Context never transfers donor eligibility, ownership, center status or progress. Predictive design activation is separate from subsequent purchased global gain.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-selected restart context changed purchases but missed the registered score gain.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment separates useful conditioning from sufficient optimization benefit. Selecting context for the actual field reduces uncertainty and changes decisions more strongly than geometric proximity alone; it also improves observed ranking on this selected stream. Those changes still produce only a small increase in global progress. Lower predictive variance did not guarantee lower overall prediction error than nearest context, and better selected-label ranking did not deliver the registered endpoint gain. The Parent comparison tests the joint addition of context selection and conditioning; passive replays cannot isolate the optimization contribution of choosing variance-based rather than nearest context because their alternative molecules were never scored.

The limiting behavior is continued local search with scarce global returns, rather than blanket restart starvation: only 19 of 989 post-reset purchases made a new global incumbent, and eight of eighteen reset episodes contributed no global gain. Molecular assessment finds recurring aromatic carbonyl, aza/dicarbonyl and cyclic-amine families; typed/generic scaffold coverage fell from 1,880/1,234 to 1,824/1,176, and within-batch similarity among nonfragment accepted molecules rose from 0.73151 to 0.73656. Fragments, oversized recombinations, unconventional heteroatom connectivity and unresolved stereochemistry persist. These observations support a limitation in the useful proposal repertoire, without proving that context selection caused the chemical liabilities or that all search collapsed to one scaffold. A proposal operator or search scheme that reaches alternative complete frameworks, or a ranking model better aligned with realized improvement, could address the remaining limitation; their benefit is untested. This node settles the registered finite-panel conversion claim and leaves the broader restart-context approach open.
finding_summary.results: The intended selection and conditioning operated at all 18 natural restarts. Every context differed from the same-state nearest-neighbor set, all 162 greedy additions lowered candidate-field variance, and all first-reset predictions became nonconstant; the Parent had 19 singleton restarts with constant first predictions. Average normalized field variance fell from 0.34138 with the root alone to 0.25660, versus 0.31394 with nearest context. Ordered purchases changed in 87 of 101 exposed announcements against owned-only predictions and 93 of 101 against nearest context. On the 989 actual post-reset labels, RMSE was 0.19675 versus 0.21031 for owned-only and 0.19557 for nearest context. Paired within-announcement rank correlation improved more often than it worsened: 52 versus 21 against owned-only, and 52 versus 39 against nearest context. All 18 restarts received first-field feedback. Post-reset global gain per evaluation increased from 0.116910/950 = 0.000123063 to 0.129368/989 = 0.000130807, while late gain mass fell from 0.832207 to 0.814778. Across all fifteen completed task/seed cells, mean score rose from 0.584614 to 0.585197, a gain of 0.000583; paired seed changes were +0.002152, -0.001374 and +0.000970. The mean remains 0.021834 below the formal Anchor. Execution and direct behavior are established, but the registered joint conversion prediction is refuted because the complete-panel score gain missed 0.002. This is a small observed gain below the criterion, not an execution failure or missing-data result.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring families and cyclic amines persist alongside N-halogen bonds, size extremes and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This is a reading of evaluated molecular output, not an activation or contribution verdict. The frozen digest, all fifteen Child Search trajectories and all fifteen published code-Parent trajectories were read. Each node supplies 4,350 optimizer observations, 870 per task; initial observations are excluded from descriptor counts. The frozen context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-7d1e6230ecce; no requested path or paired task is missing. No separate Anchor molecular comparison was performed. Only these accepted Search trajectories were used: they do not describe unpurchased candidate fields, rejected proposals, alternative histories or Confirmation/held-out behavior. The repertoire is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: 4,191 Child proposals contain perceived rings and 4,150 contain aromatic atoms. Digest ring-closure text rates range from 0.9356 to 0.9828 and aromatic-presence text rates from 0.9322 to 0.9724; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. Recognizable indole-like carbonyl/nitrile series, nitrogen-rich linked heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, phenols, ethers and conjugated dicarbonyl systems coexist with unusual annulations, N-O bonds and repeated large frameworks. All audited optimizer SMILES parse in RDKit, which establishes neither synthesis nor stability. Median size is 29 heavy atoms, with 141 below six and 254 above fifty, compared with Parent 134 and 245. There are 1,104 N-halogen-bearing proposals, 103 O-halogen-bearing proposals and 52 with O-O bonds, versus Parent 1,017, 104 and 48. These adjacency counts identify chemistry to inspect, not measured reaction hazards or universal rejection rules. Synthetic plausibility is questionable overall, while some upper-score cyclic-amine and aromatic-ketone molecules look more conventional. All Child optimizer molecules have net formal charge zero. This does not imply an absence of ionizable amines: many are present. RDKit finds potential tetrahedral centers in 2,045 proposals and assigned tetrahedral centers in none, agreeing with the digest zero stereo-marker rate. Biological activity, protonation state, stereochemical score sensitivity and synthetic routes were not measured. Child nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1,824/1,176 versus Parent 1,880/1,234. There is substantial graph variation but recurring local chemical families; these counts neither prove useful diversity nor identify which algorithm component caused a change. Every transferable gap originates in this node under the same complete frozen Search conditions. Request: policy/requests/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-7d7f7d94b7630449.json. Descriptor summary: policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/descriptor-summary.json. Each task cites its audit and actual input files; each audit pins the request, original trusted staging file, in-run byte-exact snapshot and published Parent file by SHA256. Snapshot files preserve provenance and do not expand the trusted SMILES citation set.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated molecules span 1 to 68 heavy atoms with median 26. The upper-score families are medium-sized aromatic heterocycles carrying alkoxy, nitrile and carbonyl groups. Seed 1 reaches an indole-like fused core linked through a ketone to a methylpyridyl ring; its N-bromo and N-chloro variants each have 25 heavy atoms and three rings. A closely scoring N-H analogue has 24 heavy atoms. Seed 0 instead has an aza-fused enamine-like framework, and seed 2 retains an aryl amide with N-bromination plus a chlorinated ring nitrogen. Thus carbonyl chemistry and intact ring frameworks are available, but conventional substitution is inconsistent. N-halogen-bearing proposals rise from Parent 414 to 507 of 870; typed/generic scaffolds fall from 298/161 to 276/139. Child seed-0 and seed-2 best scores exceed their Parent counterparts; seed 1 is lower. These are descriptive differences within broadly recurring families. Search sources (audit, byte-exact snapshot of trusted Child input, published Parent input): policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: N-halogenated ring nitrogens and amides raise synthetic and stability questions not answered by the score; these should not be described as ordinary carbon-halogen substitution.
The 68-heavy-atom repeated framework and small elemental fragments lack the balanced molecular architecture shown by the higher-score examples.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of a complete, bounded-size aromatic carbonyl framework is missing across the proposal stream: both fragments and repeated oversized versions remain despite the observed score separation.

A comparably explored set of conventional substitution patterns around the successful ring-and-ketone arrangements is not demonstrated. The close N-H high-score analogue shows that N-halogen bonds are not a prerequisite in the observed upper-score set; superiority of an unobserved replacement remains unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-bromo and N-chloro ketones each score 0.5193372251755369, close to the N-H methoxy/nitrile ketone at 0.5188745216627708 and above the initial aromatic amide at 0.3051048083696145. The largest repeated aromatic-ketone framework has 68 heavy atoms and scores 7.738649176226305e-72, while ClCl and C score zero. The observed gradient favors complete medium-sized aromatic carbonyl/nitrile arrangements over fragmentation or extreme repetition in these examples. It does not establish that halogenating nitrogen is necessary, or that a particular unseen pharmacophore is missing.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest typical population: median 37 heavy atoms, range 1 to 108, with 203 of 870 proposals above fifty heavy atoms. The highest observed molecule has 32 heavy atoms and six perceived rings: two related polycyclic aza-aromatic units linked through NH, with carbon-bound fluorine/bromine and methylene ring bridges. Other seed leaders contain fused imide-like dicarbonyl heterocycles or linked nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles bearing ketone and chloroalkenyl/imine side chains. Ring and aromatic text incidence are both 0.9724. The complete ordered Child and Parent SMILES sequences match in every seed, as do the descriptor populations and best structures; there is no new molecular output repertoire in this paired task. Search sources (audit, byte-exact snapshot of trusted Child input, published Parent input): policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: Large repeated heteroaromatic products create apparent route complexity; the most extreme example has 108 heavy atoms and twelve perceived rings.
Unusual annulations and multiply decorated polyheterocycles require chemistry assessment beyond validity and scaffold counts; 25 O-halogen-bearing proposals remain in the population.
missing_features: Consistent access to alternative complete frameworks that preserve the favorable linked heteroaromatic arrangement without repeated large scaffolds is not demonstrated. Scores distinguish observed arrangements, but do not identify a unique missing substituent or an unobserved objective-specific answer.

A reliably compact repertoire is lacking across the evaluated population even though the best observed framework is smaller than the population median; more aromatic rings alone does not explain the gradient.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The linked aza-aromatic leader scores 0.6366578065410841, above the initial phenyl/dicarbonyl heterocycle at 0.548381482770623. A 16-heavy-atom triazole-like molecule with unsaturated imine substituents scores 0.5118153430669254, and F, C and ClCl each score 0.5. Conversely, the 108-heavy-atom multi-indole/repeated aromatic construction scores only 0.5497404844290658. Thus the observed upper-score association is with particular connected ring/heteroatom arrangements, not monotonic growth or simply having any ring. The 0.5 values are the observed floor for these examples and do not establish useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The population spans 1 to 108 heavy atoms with median 29. Strong examples contain potentially basic tertiary amines attached to aromatic or partly saturated carbocycles: the overall best has 20 heavy atoms and three rings, with an N-propyl pyrrolidine, a benzylic connection to an indane-like phenol, and an additional aryl amino group. Other seed leaders are a dialkyl enamine-like amine attached to a dichlorophenyl-substituted cyclohexene, and a nitrogen/sulfoxide-containing ring connected to phenolic groups. Basic amine centers and saturated ring chemistry are therefore present. Seed-0 and seed-1 ordered Child/Parent molecules match; seed 2 reaches a closely related less-halogenated benzylic analogue. Its best score is 0.9999985229596998 versus Parent 0.9970518791461749. Across the task, 833 of 870 Child structures contain potential tetrahedral centers and none specifies them. N-halogen and O-halogen bonds remain in 89 and 46 proposals, respectively, even though the cited best molecule has neither. Large recombinations and lipophilic polyhalogenated analogues coexist with more conventional compact amines; no exposure or synthesis measurements establish their practical quality.
missing_features: Stereochemically explicit versions of the favorable amine-bearing ring architectures are absent even though potential centers are abundant. Whether stereochemical resolution changes this objective is untested.

Preserving the complete amine/aromatic arrangement through graph changes is inconsistent: an amine-bearing but reorganized nonaromatic endpoint is much weaker. The evidence supports an architecture-preservation gap, not a claim that the generator lacks basic ring nitrogens.

The final ketene-containing analogue scores 0.0032193675635029716, below the related seed-2 best at 0.48214377864515795. These observations favor particular moderate-size fluorinated heteroatom arrangements, not fluorine content alone, and show tolerance of N-F connectivity rather than evidence that it is chemically desirable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ded8f57a69ad, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, evaluated optimizer output only: 1,104 of 4,350 molecules have N-halogen bonds, 103 O-halogen bonds and 52 O-O bonds. The paired Parent n-7d1e6230ecce has 1,017, 104 and 48. Upper-score examples include three N-F bonds or N-brominated ring/amide nitrogens, while other strong examples lack those bonds. Audited counts are in policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/descriptor-summary.json; task-level cited structures and scores supply the associations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional heteroatom bond connectivity while elaborating recognizable ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need dependable access to conventional bond-connectivity alternatives that retain useful molecular size, functional groups and attachment geometry. Current-session feedback must determine where those alternatives matter. These output associations do not identify a component cause or prove that removing every concerning bond would improve scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ded8f57a69ad under the same frozen Search/evaluated-output conditions: 141 proposals have fewer than six heavy atoms and 254 exceed fifty, compared with Parent 134 and 245. Cited medium-sized complete molecules can score well while tiny fragments and repeated large frameworks score poorly; a 108-heavy-atom extreme is observed. This is not a universal size law. Source: policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/descriptor-summary.json and the per-task trajectory citations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably maintain complete molecular architecture while exploring size and scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic capability would need scaffold and substituent transformations that can explore both larger and smaller complete structures while preserving meaningful functional arrangements. The present data do not justify a fixed global size target, new hard filter or score-improvement claim; prospective utility must be established through accepted session feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ded8f57a69ad, the complete frozen Search panel and evaluated optimizer population: 2,045 of 4,350 molecules have RDKit-detected potential tetrahedral centers, and none has an assigned tetrahedral center. The digest independently reports zero stereo-marker rate throughout. The leading compact cyclic-amine and fluorinated partially saturated examples contain unresolved centers; Parent output has the same assignment gap. Source: policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/descriptor-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates potential stereocenters without delivering defined tetrahedral stereochemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: To supply concrete chemical candidates, a task-agnostic generator would need to represent and retain stereochemical identity through graph changes. Whether exploring those identities improves any measured objective remains untested; unspecified stereochemistry is a chemical characterization gap, not evidence of a missed score gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ded8f57a69ad versus paired n-7d1e6230ecce under the same frozen Search conditions: nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 1,824/1,176 versus 1,880/1,234. Both populations are ring-rich, yet high-score samples repeatedly use related aromatic carbonyl, aza/dicarbonyl and amine-bearing ring architectures, some with unusual annulations or reactive-looking connectivity. Counts and example associations do not measure synthetic accessibility. Source: policy/scratch/r0053-02-improve-L01-molecular/descriptor-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Extensive ring variation does not yet demonstrate reliable access to chemically interpretable alternatives outside recurring local scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need alternative complete frameworks that preserve useful functional arrangements without equating graph novelty, more rings or repeated fragments with useful chemical diversity. Score feedback and chemical interpretability need separate assessment; these descriptions neither attribute the limitation to a component nor demonstrate benefit from a specific replacement.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
